findings.message: No test checks that the web client draws the tile map. SeaScene.createTerrain (apps/web/src/seaScene.ts:97-141) builds the Phaser tilemap of land, shoal and dock tiles, but no unit or browser test reads it back. The browser helpers only sample pixels at ship positions (shipsOnCanvas, and colourAt in tests/e2e/helpers.ts:132-153). The sea.spec.ts checks on terrain (terrainAt, isNavigable) read the content module and the server readout, not the canvas. The screenshot:<id> attachments are only recorded: the verifier checks that they exist, not what they show. If createTerrain drew nothing, or put tiles in the wrong place, all four scenarios and the web unit tests would still pass. One fix would be a scenario assertion that samples canvas pixels at a known land, shoal and dock tile, using the data-camera offset, and expects each tile's placeholder colour.
findings.requirement: the web client draws the tile map

findings.message: The browser check for fog clearing along the player's path is weak. apps/web/src/web.test.ts:111-131 unit-tests FogOfWar.revealAround, which is real coverage of the path logic. The only browser check is private-match.spec.ts:29, which expects data-fog-revealed > 100 once, at spawn, before the ship moves. That attribute is FogOfWar.revealedCount, the scene's own bookkeeping, not the minimap texture. No scenario checks that the count grows as the ship sails, or that revealed minimap pixels change from the fog colour. So the per-frame wiring in SeaScene.update/revealFog and the minimap drawing are only checked for a single reveal.
findings.requirement: has a minimap whose fog clears around the player's path (client-side is fine, as terrain is public)
